FOR campaign/the-fetch -- STAGE GREEN, rc=0 in 1488 s, five rounds. The mechanical gates are satisfied and I am not raising anything further about them. One thing for your G6 package, stated once and then left alone.

WHAT FIVE ROUNDS ACHIEVED, and I want the credit accurate because you were rigorous about MECHANISM every single time: you established that the culvert failures were home-keyed instrumentation rather than lost behaviour; you re-keyed The Culvert's witness from (home,dest) to (here,dest) and left THREE graded floors where it had one; you ran a control against main to show the movement was yours and not nondeterminism; and you renamed every relaxed test honestly rather than leaving a name that lied. That is more discipline than most campaigns bring to a red.

THE ONE THING NOT IN THE PACKAGE. Across five rounds, windows/vessel/src/liveness.rs -- the file the campaign changes -- was never touched in response to a failure. Every red was answered by adjusting the witness. That can be entirely correct, and for the culvert ones you showed it was. It is unresolved for the rest:

    hot vs temperate       day 16 vs day 16       climate stopped mattering
    co-located vs apart    0 vs 0                 sharing worth nothing
    Frustrated             absent from 40 days    no straining before giving up
    the-warrant gloss      "went down to the river it knew (thirst)"
                        -> "drifted homeward, missing its people (belonging)"

I checked your ledger and retrospective for an account of that last one, since it is the most concrete: ten entries, ending at #10 (fix round 3), and the only "warrant" strings in either document are test-invocation logs. Rounds 4 and 5 are not ledgered, and the thirst errand's disappearance is not explained anywhere on the tip.

SO THE G6 QUESTION IS ONE SENTENCE, AND IT IS A WORLD QUESTION: is a world where a thirsty creature drifts homeward instead of going to the river the world this campaign intends? If yes, that is a real and defensible design change -- it deserves a decision record, and the six calibration witnesses are then measuring a world that no longer exists and should be RETIRED with a reason rather than loosened. If no, the anchor reaches past its intent, and every witness was right the first time.

Three campaigns' guards caught this independently -- The Culvert's searches floor, turn_budget's denominator, The Warrant's before-image -- none written with your campaign in mind. That convergence is evidence about the world, not about the tests.

Nothing of mine blocks you. Stage gates do not push, main is untouched at ce048e9d3, and the merge call is yours and Nathan's. I have said this four times now and this is the last; the record is on the board either way.
